newsitem.title: BELARUS: U.S. embassy protests over Belarus.
newsitem.headline: U.S. embassy protests over Belarus.

text.p: The U.S. ambassador to Belarus has protested to the former Soviet republic's authorities over expulsion from Minsk of a U.S. diplomat, an embassy spokesman told Reuters on Monday.

"The officer was carrying out normal diplomatic functions entirely in keeping with his diplomatic status and duties. The ambassador, Kenneth Yalovitz, has strongly protested this action...and he did so at the highest level of the Belarus government," the spokesman said.

Embassy first secretary Serzh Alexandrov was arrested at an anti-presidential demonstration on Sunday. State television early on Monday showed pictures of him at a police station and said he had been ordered to leave the country -- a move which the embassy spokesman said violated the Vienna convention on diplomatic rights.
"The embassy can confirm an embassy officer was unjustifiably and illegally detained on March 23 by Belarus authorities," he said.
"The highest levels of the State Department in Washington have been informed and they view this matter with the utmost seriousness and gravity.

"The embassy has demanded an immediate explanation for this arbitrary and unjustified action which again marks a further step in the movement by the government of Belarus away from democratic reforms and respect for human rights," he said.
